walkthroughs.body_html:
Light enters the eye through the pupil, passes through the lens, and lands on the retina.

The retina has rods (for dim light) and cones (for colour).

Signals travel through the optic nerve to the brain, which assembles the image - upside down at first, then flipped!

A camera works like an eye:

Lens focuses light.
Aperture controls light entry (like the pupil).
Sensor or film captures the image (like the retina).

That's why your phone's tiny lens still takes a clear photo - same physics as your eye!

Visible light is just a tiny part of the electromagnetic spectrum.

In order of energy (lowest to highest):

Radio - Microwave - Infrared - Visible - Ultraviolet - X-rays - Gamma

All travel at the speed of light. Higher-energy ones (UV, X, gamma) can be dangerous.
